en.headline: Officers confirm Tsim Sha Tsui powder letter contained flour
en.dek: Explosives officers examined a letter opened at a Humphreys Avenue commercial building and said the white powder was flour.
body: Follow-up tests on Tuesday morning's suspicious letter in Tsim Sha Tsui found no explosive material. Ming Pao reported that a security guard at 3 Humphreys Avenue opened a letter and found threatening wording and white powder, prompting police to cordon the road outside Time Fortune Commercial Building.

The Explosives Ordnance Disposal Bureau examined the powder and confirmed it was flour, with no explosive component and no immediate danger, the paper reported. Officers seized the substance for further tests. The case has been classified as criminal intimidation and passed to the Yau Tsim District support team.

The letter was addressed to the operator of a bakery in the building, Ming Pao reported, and investigators' initial understanding was that the matter might involve a money dispute. The paper said the operator later assisted police. Humphreys Avenue, closed during the examination, was later reopened.

zh.headline: 爆炸品處理課證實尖沙咀粉末信內是麵粉
zh.dek: 堪富利士道商廈保安拆信發現白色粉末及恐嚇字句，爆炸品處理課檢驗後證實是麵粉，案件列刑事恐嚇。
body: 尖沙咀周二早上的可疑信件已有進一步結果。《明報》報道，堪富利士道3號時財商業大廈一名保安員拆開信件時，發現內有恐嚇字句及白色粉末，警方接報後封鎖大廈對開路面。
報道指，爆炸品處理課人員穿上防護裝備檢驗後，證實粉末是麵粉，沒有爆炸成分，亦沒有即時危險，其後檢走作進一步化驗。案件列作刑事恐嚇，交由油尖警區支援組跟進。
《明報》稱，收件人是大廈一間烘焙店負責人，初步了解懷疑涉及金錢問題，該負責人其後在場協助警方。檢驗期間封閉的堪富利士道其後重開。
